summary: On 8 March 2023 a systemd security update applied automatically to Datadog's VMs. A restart of systemd-networkd deleted routes managed by the Cilium CNI, taking tens of thousands of nodes offline in several regions at once.

overview.background: Datadog runs Kubernetes on VMs in several cloud providers and regions. Ubuntu 22.04 images had a legacy security update channel that applied updates automatically in a window between 06:00 and 07:00 UTC.
systems: VM base image with legacy update channel
Regions US1, EU1, US3, US4, US5
Datadog platform: ingestion, monitors, web and API
overview.impact: Users could not access the platform or APIs, monitors did not alert and some data ingestion was affected. Tens of thousands of nodes went offline.
overview.severity: A multi-region outage of about a day. All services were operational by 08:58 UTC on 9 March and fully resolved on 10 March.
overview.gaps: The post gives no customer counts.

timeline.e: A systemd security update is applied automatically to VMs.
The outage begins in US1, EU1, US3, US4 and US5. Tens of thousands of nodes go offline in the next hour.
The first status page update goes out.
An update confirms impact to ingestion and monitors.
Initial signs of recovery. Web access is restored.
The first major service is declared operational.

The incident is fully resolved after historical data is backfilled.

rootCause.trigger: A systemd security update was applied automatically to a number of VMs.
rootCause.underlying: On Ubuntu 22.04 with systemd v249, restarting systemd-networkd deleted routes managed by Cilium. Fresh nodes did not show this because networkd starts before the CNI installs routes.
contributing: A legacy security update channel on the base image
A default update window that hit every region at once
Recovery needed compute, then control planes, then clusters, then services

evidence.label: The trigger
evidence.body: a security update to systemd was automatically applied to a number of VMs

evidence.label: The priority in recovery
evidence.body: Most important, usable live data and alerts are much more valuable than access to historical data.

evidence.label: A simulated networkd setting
evidence.note: Settings that tell networkd not to manage routes added by others. Shown as an example; Datadog's exact change is not published in the post.

diagnose.step: Check what changed on the nodes just before the failure.
diagnose.why: A systemd update matched the time.

diagnose.step: Compare failing nodes with fresh nodes.
Check routes on a failed node.

correct.step: Restore compute capacity region by region.
correct.why: Datadog scaled above normal in some clouds.

correct.step: Prioritise live data and alerts over history.

prevent.step: Configure networkd to leave routes unchanged.

fix.safety: Do not restart network services on production nodes as a fix without testing on one node. Restoring routes by hand across thousands of nodes needs automation.

troubleshoot.scenario: Tens of thousands of nodes lose container networking at 06:03 in four regions at once. No deploys ran.
troubleshoot.question: How do you find the cause and recover?
troubleshoot.answer: Find the automatic update, compare routes on failed and fresh nodes, restore compute, then control planes, then clusters, prioritising live data. Disable the update channel.

rootcause.q: Why did several regions fail together?
options: The same default update window applied everywhere

remediation.answer: Roll out to one region at a time with a bake time.
Compute, control planes, clusters, services, live data, history.
Verify routes after any network service restart.

design.prompt: Design a fleet whose regions cannot fail from one scheduled change.
design.answer: Immutable images, staged updates, region-specific windows, canaries and degraded-mode tests.

checks.q: What version of systemd was involved?
